title: DR1 shows each transporter's approval status as a tag — Approved or New — beside its approval number; the frontend shows no status at all, so a user cannot tell an approved transporter from an unapproved one.

finding.frontend: Each transporter is one radio, labelled with the name and hinted with the address and approval number joined by an em dash (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:92-93). Nothing on the page says whether the transporter is approved. The page heading calls them "approved commercial transporters", so a user is left to infer that everything on the list is approved — but the underlying records carry no status field to make that true (src/server/app/services/commercial-transporters/records.js:7-29), so the claim is an assumption rather than a fact the service checked.
finding.prototype: DR1's table has a Status column, and each row renders a govuk-tag: green Approved for most records, and a pink New for two of the eight (app/views/transporter.html:148-149, app/data/transporters.js). The status sits next to the approval number so a user choosing between two similar records can see which one the service has already approved, and can see when a transporter they added themselves has not been approved yet.
finding.difference: Add an approval status to each transporter record and show it on the list. The status has to come from whatever service owns the transporter register — the frontend's records are a local list with no status field, and inventing one in the frontend would mean the page asserting something nothing verified. Land the API field first, then the column.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a status, approval-state or equivalent field on the transporter records the frontend reads, whether from the local list or the service that will replace it.

relatedTo.why: The status column belongs to the list page that finding puts first
